steps.say: Every infertility workup starts with the semen sample judged against modern cut-offs, not old memories. The WHO sixth edition of 2021 sets the lower limits: volume at least 1.4 millilitres, total motility 42 percent, progressive motility 30 percent, concentration 16 million per millilitre, and normal forms 4 percent. One abnormal sample never condemns a man, so repeat after full spermatogenic cycle of ten weeks before labelling.
steps.tx: Judge semen against **WHO 2021 semen analysis** (sixth edition reference limits): volume **>=1.4 mL** (one point four millilitres), total motility **>=42%** (forty two percent), **progressive motility** (forward swimming sperm) **>=30%** (thirty percent), concentration **>=16 million/mL** (sixteen million per millilitre), and **normal morphology** (perfectly shaped sperm) **>=4%** (four percent). Repeat any abnormal sample after ten weeks, because fever, abstinence errors, and lab variation fake failure.

steps.say: Zero sperm in the ejaculate is divided into two opposite diseases with opposite treatments. Obstructive azoospermia keeps normal sized testes, normal FSH hormone, and swollen epididymides because the factory works but the pipes are blocked. Non-obstructive azoospermia shows small atrophic testes with high FSH because the factory itself has failed, so reconstruction is futile and extraction is the only road.
steps.tx: Split azoospermia by examination: **obstructive azoospermia** (blocked pipes) keeps normal testis size, normal **serum FSH** (pituitary sperm signal), and dilated epididymides, suiting reconstruction; **non-obstructive azoospermia** (failed factory) shows small atrophic testes with elevated FSH, needing extraction. This bedside split taken with one blood test directs every downstream decision, so never order genetics before classifying.

steps.say: A man born without both vas tubes carries a cystic fibrosis gene until proven otherwise. Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens flags CFTR mutations in over 95 percent of cases, so the urologist must test the man, test the partner, and counsel the couple before any sperm retrieval. Skipping genetics here risks a child with full cystic fibrosis conceived through heroic assistance.
steps.tx: Suspect **CBAVD** (absent vas tubes, congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens) with any obstructive picture and impalpable vasa: over **95%** (ninety five in a hundred) carry **CFTR mutation** (cystic fibrosis gene defect), so **cystic fibrosis** (lung and gut salt disease) counselling with partner testing is mandatory before retrieval. Document renal ultrasound too, because unilateral absence travels with missing kidneys while bilateral absence travels with CFTR.

steps.say: The Y chromosome carries its own fertility switchboard, and missing pieces predict the operating room result. Microdeletions in the AZF region on Yq11 come as AZFa, AZFb, and AZFc patterns: complete AZFa or AZFb deletions mean zero percent sperm retrieval, so surgery is refused, while AZFc deletion still yields sperm by TESE in half the cases. Karyotype plus Y deletion testing precedes every needle.
steps.tx: Map **Y-chromosome microdeletions** (missing fertility genes) in the **AZF region** (azoospermia factor zone, Yq11): complete AZFa or AZFb loss predicts **0% sperm retrieval** (no surgery offered), while **AZFc deletion** (partial loss pattern) succeeds at TESE in **50%** (fifty in a hundred). Counsel AZFc fathers that every son inherits the deletion, and test all non-obstructive men before booking theatre time.

steps.say: The commonest genetic cause of factory failure walks into clinic as a tall young man with breasts and tiny hard testes. Klinefelter syndrome, the 47 XXY karyotype, is defined by hypergonadotropic hypogonadism: the brain shouts with high gonadotropins while the testes whisper back almost no testosterone. Micro-TESE still finds sperm in half these men, so the diagnosis opens treatment rather than closing it.
steps.tx: Recognise **Klinefelter syndrome** (**47,XXY**, extra X karyotype) as the commonest genetic cause of non-obstructive azoospermia: **hypergonadotropic hypogonadism** (high brain hormones, low testosterone) with small firm testes and **gynecomastia** (breast enlargement). Start testosterone only after fertility plans complete, because exogenous hormone suppresses remaining sperm, and offer micro-TESE early since retrieval succeeds in roughly half.

steps.say: The varicocele is the commonest correctable cause of male infertility, a bag of worms above the testis cooking it a degree too warm. Microscopic subinguinal varicocelectomy ties every dilated vein under ten to fifteen times magnification while sparing the testicular arteries and lymphatics, giving the highest pregnancy rates with recurrence under 1 percent and almost no hydrocele. Loupe or laparoscopic copies are outmatched by the microscope.
steps.tx: Fix palpable varicoceles with microscopic **subinguinal varicocelectomy** (microscope vein tying): **10x-15x magnification** (ten to fifteen times zoom) with artery and **lymphatic preservation** (saving blood supply and drainage) delivers top pregnancy rates, recurrence **<1%** (under one in a hundred), and near-zero hydrocele. Reserve repair for infertility, pain, or atrophy with abnormal semen, because silent small varicoceles with normal counts earn observation.

steps.say: When the factory has only islands of production, the microscope finds them. Micro-TESE opens the testis and scans tubules at high power, plucking only the dilated opaque seminiferous tubules fat with sperm while leaving flat empty ones behind. Retrieval reaches 40 to 50 percent even in Sertoli only patterns, doubling blind biopsy yields with less tissue removed.
steps.tx: Harvest hidden production with **micro-TESE** (microscope guided extraction): operative magnification isolates dilated opaque **seminiferous tubules** (sperm filled tubes) for excision in NOA, reaching **sperm retrieval** (successful harvest) of **40% to 50%** (forty to fifty in a hundred). Targeted sampling removes less tissue than blind TESE, protecting testosterone output while doubling finds, so refer failed factory cases to micro-TESE centres.

steps.say: Blocked pipes with a healthy factory deserve replumbing, not bypass. Microsurgical vasoepididymostomy is used to join the vas directly to a single plump epididymal tubule above the blockage using the intussusception end to side technique with hair fine ten zero and eleven zero sutures. Patency returns in most men, letting conception happen in the bedroom instead of the laboratory.
steps.tx: Replumb epididymal blocks with **vasoepididymostomy** (vas to epididymis join) via the **intussusception technique** (tubule telescoped end-to-side) using **10-0 and 11-0 sutures** (microscopic stitches) from vas lumen to a single epididymal tubule. Offer it for obstructive azoospermia with healthy spermatogenesis and a palpable gap, because natural conception after patency beats a lifetime of assisted cycles.
